summary: One history corpus and one set of held-out benches, fine-tuned into Ministral-3-8B and Mistral-Small-3.2-24B with the same effective budget on one card each. The larger base answered knowledge questions better, but the triggering of abstention did not move with size; what improved was what follows an abstention, such as not inventing the missing document. An erratum notes that family and size change together in this comparison. Recipe, training figures and aggregate scores per checkpoint only (data/forge/); the lab kept no full loss curve.
title: Dataset factory, history: does a larger base help? (8B against 24B)
